questions.q: The earliest evidence of animal Husbandry and agriculture in India has come from:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The earliest evidence of animal husbandry and agriculture in the Indian subcontinent has been found at Mehrgarh (present-day Pakistan). On the basis of the latest discoveries, the earliest site with evidence of agriculture in the Indian subcontinent is Lahuradewa, located in Sant Kabir Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. Evidence of rice has been found here dating to the period between about 8000 BCE and 7000 BCE. It is noteworthy that before this latest discovery, Mehrgarh was considered the earliest agricultural site in the Indian subcontinent, where evidence of wheat has been found, while Koldihwa (on the bank of the Belan River, Prayagraj district) is considered the site with the earliest evidence of rice.

questions.q: Which one of the following periods is also known as the Chalcolithic Age?
questions.explanation: The Copper–Stone Age is also called the Chalcolithic period. Cultures in which stone tools are found in use along with copper tools are generally called Chalcolithic cultures.

questions.q: Which river valley in India was the first human fossil obtained from?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In India, the first evidence of a human fossil was found at the archaeological site of Hathnora (Sehore, Madhya Pradesh), located in the Narmada Valley. It was discovered in 1982 by Arun Sonakia, a palaeontologist of the Geological Survey of India.

questions.q: Which of the following states is the Bhimbetka site located in?
questions.explanation: The Bhimbetka archaeological site remained a centre of human activities from the Early Stone Age to the historical period. It is located in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh. Hundreds of examples of prehistoric paintings have been found in the caves of Bhimbetka. The main themes of the rock paintings include collective dance, outlined human figures, hunting, animals and birds, war, and daily activities of ancient human life. So far, about 750 rock shelters have been identified here, and paintings have been found in about 500 of them.

questions.q: Indus Civilization existed in:
questions.explanation: The historical period is determined on the basis of the knowledge of a decipherable script. The period before the knowledge of writing is called the prehistoric period. In Indian history, the period from about 3000 BC to 600 BC is considered protohistoric. The Indus Civilization belongs to the protohistoric period because writing was known here, but it has not been deciphered so far.

questions.q: What is the most significant feature of the Indus Valley Civilization?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The main feature of the Indus Valley Civilization is considered to be town planning. Here, cities and towns were established according to a fixed plan. Among the buildings made of burnt bricks, the Great Bath and the Granary of Mohenjodaro. Their surfaces were made of burnt bricks and were joined with gypsum. Buildings made of burnt bricks, planned architecture, and advanced trade and commerce were the major characteristics of this civilization. It is noteworthy that, unlike ancient civilizations such as Mesopotamia and Egypt, clear evidence of places of worship is not found in the Harappan Civilization. Similarly, the first true arch in India is seen in Balban’s tomb. Therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

questions.q: Which city is known as 'Mini Harappa'?
questions.explanation: Lothal was one of the southernmost cities of the ancient Harappan/Indus Civilization. It is also known as “Mini Harappa”. It is located in the present-day state of Gujarat. Its initial excavation was carried out under the direction of Prof. S. R. Rao.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Harappan port?
questions.explanation: The Harappan town of Lothal is located on the bank of the Bhogava River in Ahmedabad district of Gujarat. It was a Harappan-period port, from where evidence of a dockyard has been found.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Harappan site in Gujarat?

options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Lothal is in Gujarat, Kalibangan is in Rajasthan, Dabarkot is in Balochistan (Pakistan), and Rakhigarhi is in Haryana.

questions.q: Which is the oldest civilization in the world?
questions.explanation: The Mesopotamian Civilization (Iraq) is considered the oldest civilization in the world. This civilization developed in present-day Iraq and the surrounding regions. The Egyptian Civilization developed in the Nile Valley and is considered to be later than the Mesopotamian Civilization.

questions.q: Which of the following animals was not known to the people of the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.explanation: Among the given options, the people of the Indus Valley Civilization were familiar with the bull and the elephant, but scholars differ regarding the presence of the horse. It is difficult to determine with certainty whether the bones obtained from various Harappan sites belong to the wild ass/ onager (Equus hemionus khur) or to the domesticated horse (Equus caballus). Evidence of the horse, or other animals of the same group, has been reported from Rangpur, Rana Ghundai, Lothal, Surkotada, Kuntasi and Kalibangan. A scholar reported that among the so-called horse remains found from Surkotada, six were genuine horse remains dating to around 2000 BCE, i.e., around the middle of the last part of the third millennium BCE. In 1974, J.P. Joshi and A.K. Sharma of the Archaeological Survey of India reported that horse bones were found at every level here between 2100– 1700 BCE. However, Ramsharan Sharma, Romila Thapar, Mando, etc., do not accept this. Similarly, the teeth claimed to be of a horse by Brigadier E.J. Ross from the Early Harappan site of Rana Ghundai are considered inauthentic by Zauner. Therefore, regarding the horse, it would be appropriate to say that its presence in the Harappan Civilization cannot be completely denied, though its use must have been extremely limited. The Bihar Public Service Commission accepted option (b) as the answer.

questions.q: Which among the following Harappan sites was terracotta of a 'plough' was found?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the given options, terracotta replicas connected with a plough have been found from the Indus Valley sites of Banawali (Haryana) and Kalibangan (Rajasthan). According to the Archaeological Survey of India, at Kalibangan, along with a ploughed field from the early phase, a terracotta plough (replica/model) was also found. In addition, a terracotta plough (replica/model) has also been found from the ancient site of Banawali located in Fatehabad district of Haryana.

questions.q: In which of the following Harappan cities, furrows of ploughed fields have been found?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A terracotta replica/model of a plough has been found from Banawali located in Fatehabad district of Haryana. Evidence of a dockyard has been found from Lothal, situated near the Gulf of Khambhat (on the bank of the Bhogava River). Evidence of ploughed fields has been found from Kalibangan located on the bank of the Ghaggar River in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan. From Dholavira (Gujarat), a wooden signboard containing 10 large-sized signs of the Harappan script has been found.

questions.q: At which Harappan site do we find evidence of a ploughed field?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

From Dholavira (Gujarat), a wooden signboard containing 10 large-sized signs of the Harappan script has been found.

questions.q: Who among the following was not associated with the excavation of Harappa and Mohenjodaro?
questions.explanation: In 1921, Dayaram Sahni started large-scale excavation work at Harappa. From 1926–27 to 1933–34, Madho Sarup Vats remained associated with the excavation work at Harappa. Mohenjodaro was first discovered in 1922 by Rakhaldas Banerjee, who drew attention to its archaeological importance. Besides them, some other scholars—K.N. Dikshit, Ernest Mackay, Aurel Stein, A.N. Ghosh, J.P. Joshi, etc.—also made important contributions to the study of this civilization. Thus, it is clear that V.A. Smith was not associated with the excavation work related to the Harappan Civilization; rather, he was famous as an Indologist and historian.

questions.q: Which colour was commonly used in the Harappan Pottery?
questions.explanation: The people of Harappa produced earthen pots on a large scale, and traces of red colour are found on them. In the Harappan civilization, the potter’s wheel was also used to make pottery. On the basis of design, these pots were of two categories— plain (without design) pots and painted pottery. Sand was mixed with the clay used for making pottery; after firing, it took on a light brownish-red colour. The upper portion of these pots was coated with red paint, and the lower portion was decorated with various designs in black colour.

questions.q: According to the report of the IIT Kharagpur study group, continuous low rainfall for how many years was the cause of the fall of the Indus Valley Civilization?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to a report released in 2018 by a study team of the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, the Indus Valley Civilization declined due to a drought that continued for 900 years. It is noteworthy that scholars like Aurel Stein also considered climatic change to be a major reason for the decline of the Harappan civilization.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not related to the Rigvedic period?
questions.explanation: Ghosha, Apala, and Vishvavara are all female of hymns or mantras in the Rigveda, and are therefore considered to belong to the Rigvedic era. In contrast, Gargi is a philosopher of the post-Vedic/Upanishadic era, not the Rigvedic era.

questions.q: Which city served as the capital of the ancient kingdom of Magadha during the early Vedic period?
questions.explanation: During the Early Vedic period, Rajagriha (present-day Rajgir) served as the capital of the ancient Magadha empire. The first dynasty of Magadha was the Brihadratha dynasty. Brihadratha is mentioned in the Rigveda.

questions.q: Which Mandala of the Rig Veda is completely dedicated to ‘Soma’?
questions.explanation: There are a total of 10 Mandalas in the Rigveda. All 114 hymns (suktas) of the Ninth Mandala are dedicated to Soma. Soma was the main drink of the Aryans, which was obtained from the Mujavant peak. In the Tenth Mandala of the Rigveda, the origin of the four varnas is mentioned.

questions.q: To whom is the ninth Mandala of the Rigveda Samhita completely dedicated?

options.C: Deities related to plants and herbs
options.D: Soma and the deity named after this drink

questions.q: Gayatri Mantra is found in which book?
questions.explanation: The Gayatri Mantra is mentioned in the Rigveda. Its composer is Vishwamitra. This mantra is described in the Third Mandala of the Rigveda. It is dedicated to Savitr (the Sun deity).

questions.q: In which phase was the concept of untouchability was clearly put?
questions.explanation: In the period of the Dharmashastras (during the Sutra period), apart from the four varnas (Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra), many other castes also emerged in society—such as Ambashtha, Ugra, Nishad, Magadh, Vaidehak, Rathakar, etc.—as a result of anuloma and pratiloma marriages. Panini mentioned two types of Shudras—Niravasita and Aniravasita. Among these, the first type of Shudras was considered untouchable.

questions.q: When did the use of iron begin in the Indian subcontinent?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: There are differences of opinion among scholars about the beginning of iron use in the Indian subcontinent. Some scholars believe that the Hittites were the first in the world to begin using iron, and only after that did its use spread to other countries. However, excavations at the Ban Chiang archaeological site in Thailand have yielded cast iron, dated approximately to 1600–1200 BCE. In India, iron has been found from the Doab area of Noh (Rajasthan) along with Black-and-Red Ware, and its probable date is considered around 1400 BCE. The earliest clear references to this metal are found in texts of the Later Vedic period (about 1000–600 BCE.). In the Atharvaveda, iron is mentioned as “Shyama Ayas” (dark metal), and there is also a reference to an iron ploughshare. Excavations at Atranjikhera (Uttar Pradesh) have yielded the earliest agricultural iron tools along with remains of wheat, barley, and rice. Archaeologists have dated it to around 1000 BCE., which is accepted by most scholars.

questions.q: Boghaz-Koi is important because:

options.A: It was an important trading centre between Central Asia and Tibet
options.B: Inscriptions were found which mentioned the names of Vedic Gods and goddesses
options.C: Original texts of the Vedas were composed here

questions.explanation: Some inscriptions from Boghazkoi (Asia Minor) dating to the 14th century B.C. have been found. These inscriptions mention kings whose names were similar to Aryan names, and they invoked the gods Indra, Mitra, Varuna, and Nasatya as witnesses to treaties and for protection.

questions.q: Famous Battle of ‘Ten Kings’ was fought on the bank of the river:
questions.explanation: The Dasarajna War (Battle of Ten Kings) was fought on the bank of the Parushni River (modern Ravi River), in which Sudas, the king of the Bharatas, won.

questions.q: Which ancient Indian text, composed during the Later Vedic period, contains philosophical hymns and discussions on cosmology and ethics?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The Upanishads, composed during the Later Vedic period, include philosophical dialogues and discussions on cosmology and ethics. The Upanishads are ancient Indian texts written in Sanskrit, roughly between 700 BCE. and 300 BCE.

questions.q: Where was Gautam a Buddha born?
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha was born in 563 B.C. in the Lumbini grove near Kapilavastu. He attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (Bihar) on the night of Vaishakha Purnima. He delivered his first sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) at Rishipattana or Mrigdava (Sarnath) near Kashi, and he passed away at Kushinagar; this passing away is called Mahaparinirvana in Buddhist literature.

questions.q: Which Buddhist council was not held in Bihar?
questions.explanation: The First Buddhist Council was held in the Saptaparni Caves near Rajagriha (modern Rajgir) soon after the Buddha's Mahaparinirvana. The Second Buddhist Council was held in the ancient city of Vaishali. The Third Buddhist Council was held in Pataliputra (modern Patna) under the patronage of Emperor Ashoka. The Fourth Buddhist Council was probably held in Kundalvan, Kashmir. The Fourth Buddhist Council is the only one that was not held in Bihar. Therefore, the correct option is (d).

questions.q: In which city was the first Buddhist council held during the reign of Ajatashatru?
questions.explanation: The First Buddhist Council was held immediately after the death of Buddha in the Saptaparni Cave at Rajgriha (Rajgir). At that time, Ajatashatru was the ruler of Magadha. This council was presided over by Mahakassapa (Mahakashyapa), and Buddha’s chief disciples Ananda and Upali were also present. In it, Buddha’s teachings were compiled and divided into two Pitakas—Sutta and Vinaya. Ananda and Upali were considered the authorities on Dhamma and Vinaya respectively.

questions.q: A Buddhist Council during the reign of Kanishka was held at –
questions.explanation: The fourth and final Buddhist Council was held during the reign of the Kushan ruler Kanishka at Kundalvan in Kashmir. It was presided over by Vasumitra, and Ashvaghosha was its vice-president. Here, difficult portions of Buddhist texts were examined properly, and commentaries were written on each Pitaka. Kanishka got these engraved on copper plates and kept them in a stupa. These commentaries written on the Tripitaka are called “Vibhasha Shastra.” It is noteworthy that the First Buddhist Council was held immediately after Buddha’s death in the Saptaparni Cave at Rajgriha. At that time, Ajatashatru was the ruler of Magadha. It was presided over by Mahakassapa (Mahakashyapa). The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali about 100 years after Buddha’s death during the reign of Kalashoka. Its president was Acharya Sabbakami.

questions.explanation: According to the Sinhalese traditions—Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa—the Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra during Ashoka’s reign under the chairmanship of Moggaliputta Tissa.

questions.explanation: According to the Sinhalese traditions—Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa—the Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra during Ashoka’s reign under the chairmanship of Moggaliputta Tissa.

questions.q: Where did Mahatma Buddha’s ‘Mahaparinirvana’ take place?
questions.explanation: Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon at Sarnath. After that, he went to Kapilavastu, Rajgriha, Vaishali and the Kosala kingdom for the propagation of Buddhism. Buddhism was propagated the most in the Kosala kingdom. King Prasenjit of Kosala also became a disciple of Buddha along with his family. While preaching, Buddha reached Pava, the capital of the Mallas. There he stayed in the mango grove of a blacksmith named Chunda. Chunda offered him Sukaramaddava to eat; as a result, he suffered from raktatisara (bloody diarrhoea) and severe pain. Even after this suffering, he reached Kushinara (Kasia), the capital of the Malla republic. Here, in 483 B.C., at the age of 80, he passed away. In Buddhist texts, this event is called Mahaparinirvana.

questions.q: Tripitakas are the sacred books of the:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Tripitaka is the most important among Buddhist scriptures. After Buddha’s death, his teachings were compiled and divided into three parts; these are collectively called the Tripitaka. These are— 1. Vinaya Pitaka (rules related to the Sangha and a collection of conduct related to daily life), 2. Sutta Pitaka (a collection of sermons delivered by Gautama Buddha and his chief disciples), and 3. Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical doctrines of Buddhism).

questions.q: Which of the following represents a fundamental difference between Mahayana Buddhism and Hinayana Buddhism?

options.C: Worship of idols of gods and goddesses

questions.explanation: Followers of the Hinayana sect of Buddhism were not idol worshippers, whereas in the Mahayana sect, Buddha began to be regarded as a deity and the worship of his idols started. This represents the fundamental difference between the two sects of Buddhism.

questions.q: The ‘Bodhi Vriksha’ in Bodh Gaya belongs to which generation of its family?
questions.explanation: The present Bodhi Tree located at the Mahabodhi Temple is not the original tree under which Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment. According to Hiuen Tsang, the original tree was destroyed in the 7th century by Emperor Shashanka. After this, several other trees were planted at this place and were also destroyed over time. The present tree that we see is a fifth-generation tree, which was got planted by Alexander Cunningham. This tree is fully protected, and only the leaves that fall from it may be touched and picked up. According to another account, this tree was planted successively—twice by Emperor Ashoka, once by Pushyamitra Shunga, once by the King of Burma, and finally by Cunningham. Hence, it becomes a sixth-generation tree. The Tourism Department website of the Government of Bihar mentions it as a fifth-generation tree. Due to the dispute in facts, the Bihar Public Service Commission excluded this question from evaluation.

questions.q: The Chinese traveler 'Sung yun' visited India in -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Chinese traveller ‘Sung-yun’ came to India in 518 A.D. After three years of travel, he returned to China with copies of Buddhist texts.

questions.q: Gautama Buddha was elevated to the position of God during the period of:
questions.explanation: In the reign of Kanishka, at the Fourth Buddhist Council, Buddhism got clearly divided into two distinct and independent sects—Hinayana and Mahayana. In the Mahayana branch, Buddha was regarded as a deity and began to be worshipped. Along with this, the worship of many Bodhisattvas also started.

questions.q: The teachers from whom Buddha first attempted to gain enlightenment after the Mahabhinishkramana were:
questions.explanation: After the Mahabhinishkramana, in search of knowledge, Lord Buddha reached the hermitage of Alara Kalama and took initiation from him. He practised austerities there, but he was not satisfied. Alara Kalama was a teacher of Sankhya philosophy and was famous for his spiritual powers; therefore, Buddha first attempted to gain knowledge from Alara Kalama and Rudraka Ramaputra.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not common between Buddhism and Jainism?
questions.explanation: Avoidance of extremes of self-mortification (tapas) and sensual indulgence, and the adoption of the Middle Path, is followed only in Buddhism, not in Jainism. However, disbelief in the authority of the Vedas, denial of the efficacy of rituals, and prohibition of violence against living beings are found in both religions.

questions.q: Nalanda University was a great center of knowledge of -
questions.explanation: Nalanda University was world-famous for the study of Buddhist philosophy. Around the middle of the fifth century A.D., during the Gupta period, Nalanda came into existence. Kumaragupta I first donated to the Nalanda Buddhist monastery, and later Gupta rulers such as Buddhagupta, Tathagatagupta, and Baladitya also made donations to the monastery.

questions.q: Where was Mahavira Swami born?
questions.explanation: Mahavira Swami was born at Kundagrama or Kundalpur (near Vaishali) around 599 B.C. His mother Trishala was the sister of Chetaka, the chief of the Licchavi republican state of Vaishali, and his father Siddhartha was the head of the confederation of the Jnatrika Kshatriyas. His elder brother was Nandivardhana. In some old editions of National Council of Educational Research and Training books, Mahavira’s birth year is mentioned as 540 B.C. On this basis, many other publishers also printed the same year in their books, creating confusion. The correct birth year of Mahavira is 599 B.C., because Mahavira belonged to a period earlier than Gautama Buddha. Gautama Buddha was born in 563 B.C. In the newer editions of National Council of Educational Research and Training, Mahavira’s birth year is now published as 599 B.C.

questions.q: The first disciple of Lord Mahavira was –
questions.explanation: Lord Mahavira was born in 599 B.C. to Siddhartha, a feudatory of the Kshatriya lineage. His wife’s name was Yashoda, and they had a daughter named Priyadarshana. That daughter was married to Jamali, who later became a follower of Mahavira Swami. He was Mahavira’s first disciple.

questions.q: The salvation place of Mahavira, the Propounder of Jain religion, is located at -:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The place of salvation (nirvana) of Mahavira Swami—the real propounder of Jainism or the 24th Tirthankara—is located at Pavapuri. Pavapuri, situated in Nalanda district of Bihar, is a major pilgrimage site for Jains. Lord Mahavira gave up his body at Pavapuri in Bihar in 527 B.C., at the age of 72 years. In the given question, instead of “propounder of Jainism,” the wording “real propounder of Jainism” should be used, because as the propounder of Jainism, the name of Adinath or Rishabhdev is mentioned.

questions.explanation: The “14 Purvas” (Purva) are the earliest Jain texts. During the time of the last Nanda king, Sambhuta Vijay and Bhadrabahu were the heads of the Sangha. Bhadrabahu was the last person who knew the 14 Purvas given by Mahavira.

questions.explanation: Makkhali Gosala was initially a disciple of Mahavira, but later, due to differences, he gave up Mahavira’s discipleship. questions.q: The place where Mahavira attained complete spiritual knowledge (Kaivalya) is -
questions.explanation: After 12 years of severe penance and spiritual practice, Mahavira Swami attained Kaivalya (perfect knowledge) under a sal tree on the bank of the Rijupalika River near Jrimbhikagrama. As a result, he came to be known as a “Kevalin”.

questions.q: Who contributed the most to the development of the Bhagavata sect?
questions.explanation: The Bhagavata or Vaishnava religion reached its peak during the reign of the Gupta kings. questions.explanation: The Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis popularized the Bhakti religion in North India. They supported renunciation of the world. According to them, contemplation of the formless Supreme Truth and the experience of becoming one with it is the path to liberation. For this, they emphasized the need to give rigorous training to the mind and body through practices such as yogic postures, pranayama, and contemplation/meditation.

questions.explanation: According to the Puranas, the first dynasty to rule Magadha was the Brihadratha dynasty. questions.explanation: Ajatashatru (492–460 BCE), the ruler of Magadha, ascended the throne after killing his father Bimbisara, the founder of the Haryanka dynasty. He too was killed by his son Udayin (different from Udayana, the Vatsa king of Kaushambi).

questions.q: The list of sixteen Mahajanapadas is available in –
questions.explanation: In the Buddhist text Anguttara Nikaya, a list of 16 Mahajanapadas is available. These are: (1) Anga, (2) Magadha, (3) Kashi, (4) Kosala, (5) Vajji, (6) Malla, (7) Chedi, (8) Vatsa, (9) Kuru, (10) Panchala, (11) Matsya, (12) Shurasena, (13) Ashmaka, (14) Avanti, (15) Gandhara, and (16) Kamboja. Among these, only Ashmaka was located in South India. In the Buddhist text Digha Nikaya, only 12 Mahajanapadas are mentioned. The Jain text Bhagavati Sutra also gives a list of 16 Mahajanapadas, but the names differ slightly there.

Ancient Avanti was mainly the region of modern Malwa, and it had two parts: the capital of Northern Avanti was Ujjayini, and the capital of Southern Avanti was Mahishmati.

questions.q: Which dynasty did ruled over Magadha after the Nanda Dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Nanda dynasty in Magadha was established after ending the Shishunaga dynasty. There were a total of 9 kings in the Nanda dynasty. In the later period of the Nandas, the people turned against the rulers due to forcible collection of money and heavy taxes even on small items, and an atmosphere of hatred and discontent spread everywhere. Taking advantage of this situation, Chandragupta Maurya, with the help of Chanakya, killed Dhanananda and ended the Nanda dynasty. Thus, immediately after the Nandas, the Maurya dynasty was established in Magadha. After that, the Shungas, Kanvas, Guptas, etc. ruled. Therefore, as per the question, the nearest correct answer is option (a).

questions.explanation: The Chedi ruler of Kalinga, Kharavela, was one of the greatest emperors of ancient Indian history. An undated inscription of him has been found from the “Hathigumpha” cave on the Udayagiri hill in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. It gives a chronological account of events from Kharavela’s childhood, education, coronation, and the events of the first thirteen years of his reign. questions.q: The capital of Anga Janapada was-
questions.explanation: The present districts of Bhagalpur and Munger in southern Bihar were included in the Anga Mahajanapada. Its capital was Champa. questions.q: Which one of the following rulers of Magadha was the contemporary of Alexander, the Great?
questions.explanation: The last ruler of the Nanda dynasty was Dhanananda, who was a contemporary of Alexander. Greek writers called him Agrammes. Xenophon describes him as a very wealthy person. Bhaddasala was his commander-in-chief.

questions.q: Who recognized Sandrokottos as Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: William Jones was the first scholar who identified Sandrokottas (Sandrocottus) with the Mauryan ruler Chandragupta Maurya. Appian and Plutarch described Chandragupta Maurya as Androkottas/Androcottus, while Justin, Strabo, and Arrian mentioned him as Sandrokottas (Sandrocottus). options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

He was the first emperor who established his rule over a vast territory, and the extent of his empire was larger than the British Indian Empire. The boundary of his empire touched Iran. He was the first to politically unify India.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
questions.explanation: The Maurya dynasty was founded by Chandragupta Maurya. Its period was 321–184 BCE. After this, the Kushana dynasty, the Gupta dynasty, and the Vardhana dynasty ruled ancient India.

questions.q: Who amongst the following Mauryan rulers did conquered the Deccan?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan Empire, conquered South India (the Deccan). In this regard, information is obtained from Ashoka’s inscriptions, and from Jain and Tamil sources. Ashoka’s inscriptions are found at many places in the southern region, but Ashoka carried out only the Kalinga conquest. Therefore, the credit for conquest in the south has to be given to Chandragupta Maurya, because Bindusara’s conquests are highly doubtful and he is not remembered in history as a conqueror. Jain and Tamil sources also confirm Chandragupta Maurya’s southern conquest.

In Mudrarakshasa, Chandragupta is also called “Vrishala” and “Kulheen.” In the 18th century CE, Dhundhiraj wrote a commentary on Mudrarakshasa.

questions.explanation: Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the royal court of Chandragupta Maurya. Earlier, he had served as Seleucus’s envoy in the royal court of the satrap of Arachosia.

questions.q: In how many categories did Megasthenes divide the Indian society?
questions.explanation: In his book Indica, Megasthenes divided Indian society into seven categories—(1) Philosophers, (2) Farmers, (3) Herders, (4) Craftsmen and businessmen, (5) Warriors, (6) Inspectors, and (7) Ministers and preachers. Megasthenes does not mention the prevalence of slavery in Indian society. In the Mauryan period, no person could marry outside his caste, nor could he adopt an occupation different from it.

questions.q: The central point in Ashoka's Dhamma is -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Ashoka’s Dhamma (Dharma) was a moral code. Through his second and seventh pillar edicts, Ashoka conveys the message—“Apasinave bahukayane daya dane, sache sochaye madave sadhave cha.” That is, do less wrongdoing, do welfare, show compassion and charity, speak the truth, live with purity, maintain gentleness in nature, and uphold goodness. Thus, the basic message of Ashoka’s Dhamma includes peace and nonviolence, respect for elders, and religious tolerance. Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

questions.q: Language used in the inscriptions of Ashoka is:
questions.explanation: Ashoka’s history is known mainly from his inscriptions. His inscriptions can be classified into three categories—(1) Rock Edicts, (2) Pillar Edicts, and (3) Cave Inscriptions. questions.q: Which inscription tells about the various achievements of Rudradaman-I?
questions.explanation: An inscription of Rudradaman I has been found at Junagadh (Gujarat). The same rock on which it is engraved also contains a copy of Ashoka’s fourteen major rock edicts and an inscription of Skandagupta. It is written in pure Sanskrit and in the Brahmi script. It throws light on Rudradaman’s various achievements

questions.q: According to the rock inscription in Sanskrit, composed around the second century CE, Sudarshan Lake, an artificial reservoir, was repaired by

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I (130–150 CE) has been found from Girnar Hill in Gujarat. This Sanskrit inscription is among the early Sanskrit inscriptions. From it, we get information about the construction and reconstruction of the dam of Sudarshana Lake.

questions.q: Who among the following first issued gold coins on a large scale?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The introduction of gold coinage on a large scale by the Kushana rulers was their most important contribution to the Indian subcontinent. Vima Kadphises is credited with starting the circulation of gold coins.

questions.q: In pre-Gupta times, a large number of lead coins were issued by the

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the pre-Gupta period, a large number of lead coins were issued by the Satavahana rulers. It may be noted that the Satavahana dynasty was founded by Simuka. Their actual capital was Pratishthana (Paithan). In the Puranas, this dynasty is called Andhrabhritya or of Andhra origin.

questions.q: Which dynasty ruled over India after the Shunga dynasty?
questions.explanation: The last Shunga king, Devabhuti, was killed through the conspiracies of his minister Vasudeva. The new dynasty founded by Vasudeva came to be known as the Kanva or Kanvayana dynasty. Like the Shungas, it was also a Brahmin dynasty.

questions.q: Which Gupta ruler assumed the throne after killing his elder brother?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: After Samudragupta, his son Ramagupta became the ruler. However, since he could not effectively resist the Shaka invasions, his brother Chandragupta II killed Ramagupta, married his wife Dhruvadevi, and achieved victory over the Shakas.

questions.q: Who is called ‘the Napoleon of Ancient India’?
questions.explanation: Historian Vincent Smith, impressed by Samudragupta’s valour and conquests, gave him the title ‘Indian Napoleon’ in his work The Early History of India. Samudragupta’s conquests are described in the Prayag-Prashasti. Its author was Harishena.

questions.q: The Gupta emperor who defeated the ‘Hunas’ was:
questions.explanation: The first Huna invasion of India took place during the reign of the Gupta emperor Skandagupta (around 455 CE), and they were badly defeated by him. This invasion was only a raid and had no major direct impact on the country; however, indirectly it accelerated the decline of the Gupta Empire. After Skandagupta’s death, in the late 5th century and the beginning of the 6th century, the Hunas captured several regions in the north-west.

questions.q: Who was the founder of Nalanda University?
questions.explanation: According to Hiuen Tsang, the founder of Nalanda University was ‘Shakraditya’, who established it due to his great devotion to Buddhism. Shakraditya is identified with the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I (415–455 CE). Kumaragupta’s famous title was ‘Mahendraditya’. Nalanda was a renowned Buddhist centre and university. It was located near Rajgir in southern Bihar. Even today, its ruins are scattered far and wide around the village of Bargaon. In the mid-5th century, during the Gupta period, Nalanda University came into existence. Kumaragupta I was the first to donate to the Nalanda Buddhist Vihara, and later Gupta rulers such as Buddhagupta and Baladitya also made donations to this vihara.

questions.q: Nalanda University was founded during the dynasty of
questions.explanation: According to Hiuen Tsang, the founder of Nalanda University was ‘Shakraditya’, who established it due to his great devotion to Buddhism. Shakraditya is identified with the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I (415–455 CE). Kumaragupta’s famous title was ‘Mahendraditya’. Nalanda was a renowned Buddhist centre and university. It was located near Rajgir in southern Bihar. Even today, its ruins are scattered far and wide around the village of Bargaon. In the mid-5th century, during the Gupta period, Nalanda University came into existence. Kumaragupta I was the first to donate to the Nalanda Buddhist Vihara, and later Gupta rulers such as Buddhagupta and Baladitya also made donations to this vihara.

questions.q: Who among the following was not an Acharya in the Nalanda Vishvavidyalaya?
questions.explanation: Kautilya (Chanakya) is considered to have been a teacher of the 4th-3rd centuries BCE, a prime minister during the reigns of the Mauryan emperors Chandragupta Maurya and Bindusara, and author of the Arthashastra. According to tradition, he was an expert associated with Takshashila, while the systematic development of Nalanda Mahavihara occurred during the Gupta period.

questions.q: Why was Nalanda University famous in the world?
questions.explanation: Nalanda University was world-famous for the study of Buddhist philosophy. The Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang came to India to study there.

questions.q: Out of two statements below first is Assertion(A) and second is Reason (R), carefully read both statements. Assertion (A) : Till the end of the twelfth century Nalanda Mahavihara lost its glory. Reason (R) : State protection ceased to be available to the Mahavihara. With respect to the above-mentioned two statements, which of the following is true?

options.A: (A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.B: (A) and (R) both are true, and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation: Nalanda was a renowned Buddhist centre and university. It was located near Rajgir (ancient name: Rajgriha) in southern Bihar. The university at Nalanda came into existence in the mid-5th century during the time of the Gupta rulers. In the last decade of the 12th century, as a result of Muslim invasions, this Mahavihara declined. Also, because the Pala rulers of Bengal patronised Vikramashila University, the importance of Nalanda began to diminish.

questions.q: Consider the following statements : 1. Fa-Hien was a Chinese pilgrim who visited India during the reign of Harsha. 2. Hiuen Tsang was a Chinese Buddhist monk who visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Fa-Hien was a Chinese traveler, and he visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II. He wrote a detailed account of the life of the people here. In his account, he did not mention the king’s name. The Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of Emperor Harsha. He described the multi-storeyed bronze monastery built by Harsha at Nalanda. In his account, he mentioned that during Harsha’s period the Shudras practiced agriculture. He also mentioned the assembly held at Prayagraj (Prayag) in his travelogue. Therefore, both statement (1) and statement (2) are incorrect.

questions.q: The famous Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Fa-Hien was a Chinese traveler, and he visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II. He wrote a detailed account of the life of the people here. In his account, he did not mention the king’s name. The Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of Emperor Harsha. He described the multi-storeyed bronze monastery built by Harsha at Nalanda. In his account, he mentioned that during Harsha’s period the Shudras practiced agriculture. He also mentioned the assembly held at Prayagraj (Prayag) in his travelogue. Therefore, both statement (1) and statement (2) are incorrect.

questions.q: The gradual decline of towns was an important feature of which period?
questions.explanation: In the Gupta period, towns moved towards gradual decline. Across the entire Ganga valley, many cities that were earlier extremely prosperous were either abandoned in the Gupta age or witnessed considerable disruption in settlement. By the time of Xuanzang’s arrival, even an important city like Pataliputra had turned into a village. Important towns like Mathura, and places such as Kumhrar, Sonpur, Sohgaura, and many significant centers of the Ganga valley in Uttar Pradesh also show clear evidence of decline.

questions.q: Which one of the following ports was in use for the North Indian trade during the Gupta period?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: During the Gupta period, Tamralipti in Bengal was a major port, from where North India traded with South-East Asia, China, Lanka, Java, Sumatra, etc. The major port of western India was Bhrigukachchha (Bharuch), from where maritime trade took place with western countries. Besides this, Kalyan and Cambay were also used for North Indian trade.

questions.q: Which ruling dynasty donated the maximum villages to temples and Brahmins?
questions.explanation: The rulers of the Gupta dynasty gave the maximum number of village grants to temples and Brahmins. The land grants mentioned in Gupta inscriptions make it clear that along with the land grant, the income generated from the village land was also handed over to the recipient.

questions.q: What was the land revenue rate in the Gupta age?
questions.explanation: In the Gupta period, those who cultivated on state land had to pay a part of their produce (one-sixth of the produce) to the king as tax, which was called Shashthansh (one-sixth). In Gupta inscriptions, this land tax is referred to as ‘Bhagkar’ or ‘Udrang’.

questions.q: What is the rate of land revenue in the Dharmashastras?
questions.explanation: In almost all Dharmashastra texts, the rate of land revenue was 1/6 (one-sixth of the produce).

questions.q: What type of land was called ‘Aprahata’?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Unploughed wild land (land on which cultivation has not been done) was called ‘Aprahata land’. This is a term of the Gupta-period revenue system.

questions.q: Consider the types of land according to the Amarkosha: (A) Urvara-fertile (B) Maru-desert (C) Shadvala-grassy (D) Devamatrika-watered by rain Which of the following is correct ?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Amara Singh one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) of Chandragupta II ‘Vikramaditya’, composed the work titled ‘Amarakosha’. Amarakosha gives a list of 12 types of land, including—Urvara (fertile land), Maru (desert land), Ushara (barren land), Aprahata (fallow land), Shadvala/Shadbala (grass land), Pankila (muddy land), Jalaprayanupama (moist land), Kaccha (marshy land/land near water sources), Sharkara (limestone/pebble-bearing land), Sharkaravati (sandy land), Nadimatrika (river-irrigated land) and Devamatrika (rain-fed). Hence, all the matchings given in the options are correct. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q: Who was the author of the famous ‘Allahabad Prashasti’?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The author of the famous Allahabad Prashasti was Harishena. On the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad (presentday Prayagraj), Harishena presented a eulogistic account of Samudragupta, which is called the ‘Prayag Prashasti’. In the same Prashasti, Harishena described himself as Sandhivigrahika, Kumaramatya and Dandanayaka. This implies that in the Gupta period, a person could be appointed to more than one post.

questions.q: In the Puranas, the rulers of which dynasty were called ‘Shriparvatiya’?
questions.explanation: In the Puranas, the rulers of the Ikshvaku dynasty are called ‘Shriparvatiya’ (rulers of the Shriparvata region) and ‘Andhrabhritya’ (servants of the Andhras). Earlier, they were feudatories of the Satavahanas, but after their decline they declared independence. The founder of this dynasty was Shri Shantamula.

questions.q: Consider the following about the King “Pravaerasena” : (A) He was the real founder of the Vakataka dynasty. (B) His empire extended from Bundelkhand in the north to Hyderabad in the South. (C) He succeeded his father king Vindhyashakti. (D) He is mentioned in the Puranas. Which of the following statements are correct ?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Vakataka dynasty was an ancient Indian dynasty that ruled the central and southern parts of India from the 3rd century CE to the end of the 5th century CE / beginning of the 6th century CE. The founder of this dynasty was Vindhyashakti I, whose successor was Pravarasena I, who is also called the real founder of the Vakataka dynasty. During the time of Pravarasena I, the boundaries of the Vakataka kingdom expanded from the Vindhya region in the north (the present Bundelkhand region is included in this) to the Deccan in the south (present Hyderabad also fell within his sphere of influence). Among the Vakataka rulers, he was the first to assume the title of ‘Samrat’ and performed four Ashvamedha sacrifices and other Vedic rituals. In the Puranas, he is referred to as ‘Praveera’. Hence, all four statements are true.

questions.q: The Huna King Toramana was defeated by the Aulikara King

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Huna king Toramana was defeated by the Aulikara king Prakashadharman. After the death of Skandagupta, the Hunas again attacked the Ganga valley. The leader of this second Huna invasion was Toramana. His inscription has been found engraved on a Varaha (boar) image at Eran in Central India. Two seals of Toramana have been found at Kaushambi. Toramana appointed his son Mihirakula as his successor.

questions.q: Who laid the foundation of the Vardhana Dynasty?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to Banabhatta’s work Harshacharita, the Vardhana dynasty was founded by a person named Pushyabhuti at Thaneshwar/Sthaneshwar. Harshavardhana was the greatest ruler of this dynasty.

questions.q: Poet Bana was an inhabitant of –
questions.explanation: There is considerable disagreement among scholars regarding the birthplace of Banabhatta. According to some scholars, he was born in a village named Pritikuta located on the bank of the Son River in Bihar, while others believe he was born in a village named Pritikut near Kanyakubja (Kannauj) in Uttar Pradesh. His father’s name was Chitrabhanu and his mother’s name was Rajadevi.

questions.q: Which Chinese traveller visited India during Harshavardhana’s rule?
questions.explanation: The most important event of Harshavardhana’s time was the arrival of the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang in India. His strong desire was to see the places made sacred by the footprints of Gautama Buddha and to study the sacred Buddhist texts, which were available in India in those days. To fulfil this aim, he left Chang'an (Changan), the capital of the Tang rulers, for India in 629 CE. He wrote a book about his Indian journey, known as Si-Yu-Ki.

questions.q: Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang studied at the University of –
questions.explanation: In 637 CE, Hiuen Tsang went to Nalanda University. At that time, the Vice-Chancellor there was Acharya Shilabhadra. He stayed at Nalanda for about 15 months and studied Yogashastra under Acharya Shilabhadra. After this, he reached Kanchi via Bengal, Odisha and Dhanyakataka. In the second phase of his journey, Hiuen Tsang again came to Nalanda in 642 CE. Thus, the total period of his stay at Nalanda (combining both visits) was about two years.

questions.q: During Hiuen-Tsang tour in India the most famous city for the production of cotton clothes was:
questions.explanation: The Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang came to India during the time of Harshavardhana (606–647 CE). According to him, Mathura was famous for cotton textiles at that time, whereas Varanasi was famous for silk textiles. He also states that the main reason for the prosperity of Thaneshwar was trade. Bana described the city of Thaneshwar as a “land of wishfulfilment” for guests and a “red land” for merchants. Most of its inhabitants were traders who dealt in various goods. Ujjayini and Kannauj were also very prosperous economically during this period.

questions.q: Which of the following rulers ruled Assam during the time of Harsha?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the given options, during Harsha’s time, Bhaskar Varman ruled Assam. Bhaskar Varman was a ruler of the Varman dynasty in Kamarupa (Assam). According to Mukunda Madhava Sharma’s book 'Inscription of Ancient Assam' and the Assam Gazetteer, after Bhaskar Varman, for a few years Avanti Varman became the ruler; Salastambha removed him from the throne and seized the throne.

questions.q: Who was the ruler of India during the 7th century CE known for his patronage of Buddhism and support for cultural activities?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: During the 7th century AD, Harsha (Harshavardhana), a ruler of the Pushyabhuti dynasty, is known for patronizing Buddhism and supporting cultural activities. Harshavardhana ruled from about 606 AD to about 647 AD (about 41 years).

questions.q: During the Gupta-Vakataka Era, which important school of Indian philosophy developed, focusing on logical reasoning and debate?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In the Gupta–Vakataka age, the school of Indian philosophy that developed with a focus on logical reasoning and debate was Nyaya. The founder of Nyaya philosophy is Gautama. According to Nyaya, knowledge can be valid or invalid. Valid knowledge is called Prama, and invalid knowledge is called Aprama.

questions.q: Who among these was the first to explain that the daily sunrise and sunset occur due to the Earth's rotation on its axis?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Aryabhatta was the first person to explain that the daily sunrise and sunset occur because the Earth rotates on its axis.

questions.q: Who among the following is known for his work on medicine during the Gupta period?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sushruta is called the “Father of Surgery.” He was from Kashi, and his period is generally considered to be about 1000 BC to 600 BC. Shaunaka was a sage of the Rigvedic period. Shudraka was a Gupta-period playwright. Saumila is a Gupta-period playwright, whom Kalidasa mentions along with Bhasa and Kaviputra. Thus, in the Gupta period, none of the above worked in the field of medicine. However, the Bihar Public Service Commission, in both its preliminary and final answer keys, considered option (a) as the correct answer. Since the Gupta period begins from 275 AD (Sri Gupta), which is about 1000 years after the accepted period of Sushruta (about 1000 BC to 600 BC), it is not reasonable to consider Sushruta as a contemporary of the Gupta period.

questions.q: Who used the caves of Barabar as their shelter-house?
questions.explanation: In the Mauryan age, the art of cutting hills to make residential caves developed. During the time of Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha, caves were cut in the Barabar and Nagarjuni hills to provide dwellings for the Ajivikas. In Ashoka’s time, the prominent caves in the Barabar hills included the “Sudama Cave,” “Karna Chaupar,” etc.

questions.q: In Indian art, the construction of ‘Stupa’, ‘Chaitya’ and ‘Vihara’ is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: In Indian architecture, stupa, chaitya and vihara are the major elements of Buddhist architecture. A stupa is a hemispherical memorial structure in which the bodily relics of Gautama Buddha and his close disciples were mainly enshrined. A stupa is a place of worship, but it does not have a separate worship chamber. A chaitya is a prayer hall that includes a worship hall and a stupa; Buddhist monks used to sit in this hall and perform worship. A vihara is the residential monastery of Buddhist monks, used for study, rest and meditation.

questions.q: The associates of Khajuraho Temple Architecture were –
questions.explanation: The temples built by the Chandela kings at Khajuraho, located in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh, still testify to the excellence of Chandela architecture. These temples were mainly constructed between the 10th and 11th centuries, i.e., around 950–1050 CE (the main period of the Chandelas, though construction also took place in earlier and later phases). Among the temples here, the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is the most prominent.

questions.q: Art of Gandhara style flourished during the reign of –
questions.explanation: The Gandhara school of art developed mainly during the Kushana period. Under this art tradition, a large number of images of Buddha were produced.

questions.q: The oldest sculpture of Buddha is made in which style?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: During the Kushana period, a large number of statues of Buddha and Bodhisattvas (both seated and standing) were produced under the Gandhara and Mathura schools. According to V.S. Agrawal, Buddha images were first made at Mathura, where a suitable base for their development existed. According to Xuanzang’s account, the first image of Buddha was made at Kaushambi; however, many scholars credit the Gandhara school with the earliest Buddha image. In its final answer key, the Bihar Public Service Commission accepted option (a) as the correct answer.

questions.q: The temple of Deogarh near Jhansi and the sculptures in the temple at Garwha near Allahabad (Prayagraj) are the important remains of the which art?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh (presently in Lalitpur district of Uttar Pradesh) is a Gupta-period temple. Similarly, the Garhwa Temple located in the Garhwa fort at Allahabad (Prayagraj) is also of the Gupta period.

questions.q: The painting of ‘Bodhisattva Padmapani’ is located at
questions.explanation: The painting of Bodhisattva Padmapani (Avalokiteshvara) is located at Ajanta. Notably, this extraordinary mural dates roughly to the mid-5th to 6th century CE and is preserved in the interior of the rock-cut Buddhist monastic complex at Ajanta. It also provides early visual evidence of elaborate crowns worn as indicators of both royal and divine status.

questions.q: In which of the following inscriptions is an example of widow-burning mentioned?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An example of widow-burning (Sati) is found in the Eran pillar inscription of Bhanugupta. This inscription mentions that after Goparaja, a minister of Bhanugupta, died in a battle, his wife performed Sati. The inscription is dated to 510 CE. Eran is a historic village located in Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh, situated at the confluence of the Bina and Reuta (Ruta) rivers.

questions.q: The contributors in the construction of Khajuraho temple architecture were—
questions.explanation: The temples built by the Chandela kings at Khajuraho, located in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh, still testify to the excellence of Chandela architecture. These temples were mainly constructed between the 10th and 11th centuries, i.e., around 950–1050 CE (the main period of the Chandelas, though construction also took place in earlier and later phases). Among the temples here, the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is the most prominent.

questions.q: Borobudur is the most amazing stupa in the world and whose magnificent example is its statue and sculpture?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Borobudur (Borobudur/Barabudur) Stupa is situated on the island of Java in Indonesia. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q: According to Chinese source, Meghavarman, the ruler of Sri Lanka, sent a missionary to which of the following Gupta Kings for permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya?
questions.explanation: Meghavarman sent an envoy to Samudragupta seeking permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya. Samudragupta granted the Sri Lankan (Ceylonese) Buddhist king Meghavarman permission to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya. - 8

chapters.chapter_name: South India (Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Sangam Period)

questions.q: Who was the founder of Chola dynasty?

options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Chola empire was founded by Vijayalaya, who initially was a feudatory chief of the Pallavas. Around 850 CE, he captured Tanjore. The Shaiva temple at Tanjore— Rajarajeshwara (or Brihadishwara) Temple—was built during the reign of Rajaraja I.

questions.q: The Chola age was most famous for:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The most notable feature of Chola rule is seen in the functioning of autonomous village institutions. In fact, during this period, villages were complete units of local selfgovernment, and village administration was carried out by the villagers themselves.

questions.q: Which medieval Indian empire was famous for elaborate local self-government?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The most notable feature of Chola rule is seen in the functioning of autonomous village institutions. In fact, during this period, villages were complete units of local selfgovernment, and village administration was carried out by the villagers themselves.

questions.q: Which dynasty built the Kailasanatha Temple and in which state?
questions.explanation: The Kailasanatha (Kailasanathar) Temple is located in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu. It was built under the patronage of the Pallava rulers.

questions.q: Which of the following temples is located in Kanchipuram?
questions.explanation: Ekambareswarar Temple is located in Kanchipuram. It is dedicated to Mahadeva (Shiva). The temple was built during the period of the Pallava rulers. It is noteworthy that this temple is thousands of years old. Various inscriptions from the Pallava period to the period of the Nayaka rulers have been found here. On the basis of available archaeological evidence, it can be said that the major construction work of this temple was carried out during the times of the Pallavas, the Cholas, and the Vijayanagara rulers.

questions.q: The Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur was constructed by which king?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Brihadeeswarar Temple is a Hindu temple located in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu, built in the early 11th century. The temple was constructed between 1003 and 1010 CE by the Chola ruler Rajaraja I. It is also known as the Rajarajeshwara Temple. The temple was built in the Dravidian style of architecture.

questions.q: Which of the following was the capital of the Chera dynasty ?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Chera dynasty ruled the south-western part of South India (present-day Kerala and some parts of Tamil Nadu). According to the Kerala State Gazetteer, the Cheras’ capital Vanchi is also mentioned, which some scholars identify with Karur/Kuruvur. The earliest Chera king whose name is first mentioned in sources was Udayanjeral (Uthiyan Cheral).

questions.q: Which of the following dynasties is not mentioned in Sangam literature?
questions.explanation: Sangam literature provides accounts of the origin and development of the Chola, Chera, and Pandya rulers. Even though fixing the exact reign periods of various kings is difficult, Sangam literature throws sufficient light on political activities from the south of the Krishna River up to the far southern peninsula. The Kadamba dynasty is not mentioned in Sangam literature.

questions.q: Why was ‘Uraiyur’ famous in Sangam Era?

options.A: An important trade centre of spices
options.B: An important trade centre of cotton
options.C: An important centre of foreign trade
options.D: An important centre of domestic trade

questions.explanation: Uraiyur was an important Sangam-period city situated on the banks of the Kaveri River in Tiruchirappalli (Tamil Nadu). In the Sangam age, Uraiyur was a major centre for cotton textiles. In the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, it is mentioned by the name Argaru.

questions.q: The attractive doors of the temples of South India are called-

options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The attractive gateway of South Indian temples is called 'Gopuram'. The Dravidian style flourished during the Pallava, Pandya, and Chola periods. In the Pandya period, temples were comparatively small, but many enclosure walls were built around their courtyards. Their entrance gateways, called gopurams, later became grand, massive structures richly decorated with sculpture. The Chola rulers built magnificent temples as well as huge gopurams.

questions.q: Who established trade relations with Roman Empire?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: India’s trade with the Roman Empire began during the Sangam period with the Chera state. Many Roman objects have been found from Arikamedu.

questions.q: During whose reign did the Persian traveller ‘Abdur Razzaq’ come to India?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq came to Vijayanagar during the reign of Devaraya II (tenure: 1422–1446 CE), the most powerful ruler of the Sangama dynasty. In his travel account Matla’ al-Sa‘dayn wa Majma‘ al-Bahrayn, he described the reign of Devaraya II.

questions.q: Which of the following Indian Philosophies has given the theory of atom?

options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the Vaiseshika school, the material world is composed of atoms. Maharshi Kanada was the propounder of this school of philosophy.

questions.q: In Kalidasa's 'Kumarasambhavam', what mythological character's birth story is found?
questions.explanation: Kalidasa’s Sanskrit epic “Kumarasambhava” narrates the birth story of Kumar (also known as Kartikeya/Skanda), the son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati.

questions.q: Who of the following was the writer of Mudrarakshasa?
questions.explanation: “Mudrarakshasa” was written by Vishakhadatta. This work throws light on Mauryan history, mainly on the life of Chandragupta Maurya.

questions.q: What is the name of Megasthenes’ book?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya was a contemporary of Alexander. Foreign writers contemporary to Alexander include Nearchus, Onesicritus, Aristobulus, and Megasthenes, whose accounts provide information about Chandragupta Maurya. Among these foreign writers, Megasthenes is the most important, and his book “Indica” is a major source for Mauryan history. In “Indica”, Megasthenes describes the municipal administration of Pataliputra. According to him, the administration of the city was carried out through committees comprising a total of 30 members. There were 6 committees in all, and each committee had 5 members. One committee was responsible for collecting sales tax. Sales tax was collected as one-tenth of the value. Those who evaded taxes were awarded the death penalty.

questions.explanation: Kalhana wrote the history of Kashmir in Rajatarangini. He composed this work during the reign of Jayasimha (1128– 1149 AD). Chanakya (Kautilya), the Prime Minister of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the famous treatise Arthashastra on political science.

questions.q: Kautilya's Arthashastra is a book based on -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Arthashastra, written by Kautilya (Chanakya) during the Mauryan period, is a book on the principles and practice of governance. It explains the Mandala theory of the state, which discusses foreign policy. It also describes the Saptanga theory—Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda, and Mitra. The Arthashastra also gives detailed information about the administration of that time, as well as agriculture, crafts, and trade.

questions.q: Kautilya’s Arthashastra deals with the aspects of –
questions.explanation: Through Kautilya’s Arthashastra, we learn many things about the Mauryan administration. It is not actually a historical text; rather, it is a unique treatise on political science. It mainly focuses on political policies.

questions.q: Who was the author of the book 'Arthashastra'?

questions.q: Which pair correctly matches the kings of the ancient and medieval periods of history with the works written by them?
questions.explanation: The correct pairs are as follows— Mattavilasaprahasana — Mahendravarman I Amuktamalyada — Krishnadeva Raya Samaranganasutradhara — King Bhoja (Paramara dynasty) Manasollasa — Someshwara III

questions.q: Who wrote 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea is a Greco-Roman work. It describes navigation routes and trade opportunities from the ports of Roman Egypt. It was written around 60 AD by an anonymous merchant. It also mentions the goods imported and exported to and from India.

questions.q: The author of ‘Prithviraj Raso’ is –
questions.explanation: Chand Bardai, the court poet of the Chauhan ruler Prithviraj III (Rayapithora), composed Prithviraj Raso. In it, the Chauhans are described as having originated from the fire-pit (Agnikunda).

questions.q: Who wrote the book 'Prithviraj Raso'?
questions.explanation: Chand Bardai, the court poet of the Chauhan ruler Prithviraj III (Rayapithora), composed Prithviraj Raso. In it, the Chauhans are described as having originated from the fire-pit (Agnikunda).

questions.q: The author of ‘Swapnavasavadatta’ is
questions.explanation: Thirteen plays are attributed to the great poet Bhasa. These were obtained from the Travancore State in 1909 by T. Ganapati Shastri, and were published in 1912. The names of these plays are— (1) Pratijna-Yaugandharayana, (2) Swapnavasavadatta, (3) Urubhanga, (4) Duta-Vakyam, (5) Pancharatram, (6) Balacharita, (7) Duta-Ghatotkacha, (8) Karnabhara, (9) Madhyamavyayoga, (10) Pratimanatakam, (11) Abhisheka- Natakam, (12) Avimarakam, and (13) Charudatta.

questions.q: ‘Kumarasambhava,’ an epic poem was composed by –
questions.explanation: The epic Kumarasambhavam was composed by the great poet Kalidasa. It has 17 cantos (only the first eight cantos were written by Kalidasa; the remaining nine cantos were written by other poets). It contains vivid description of nature and narrates the birth of Kartikeya and the slaying of Tarakasura.

questions.q: Who wrote the book “Kiratarjuniya”?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The author of Kiratarjuniya is Bharavi. Its plot is taken from the Mahabharata. It describes the battle between Arjuna and Shiva, who appears disguised as a Kirata.

questions.q: Name the source that is silent about the trade routes of ancient India:
questions.explanation: This text, written in the Pali language, describes a dialogue between Nagasena and the Indo-Greek ruler Menander. It does not contain a description of trade routes.

questions.q: Who wrote the book 'Harshacharita'?
questions.explanation: Harshacharita was written by the famous author Banabhatta. It is a major source for the history of the Vardhana dynasty. It is an akhyayika (a biographical narrative) in which the author presents the life of his contemporary ruler and the ruler’s ancestors.

questions.q: Nitisara, an early book of politics, was written by
questions.explanation: Nitisara, composed by Kamandaka, is an important collection of 1,192 verses (shlokas). It is arranged into 34 sections (prakaranas) and 20 chapters or cantos (sargas). It includes the traditional branches of learning: the state, its constituents and protection, the Mandala theory of interstate relations, various kinds of policies, war and peace, diplomacy and wisdom, military organization, and the faults that should be avoided. The appendix lists, for comparison, the contents of Kautilya’s Arthashastra and Kamandaka’s Nitisara.

questions.q: Who was the founder of the Karnata dynasty?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Nanyadeva (1097–1147 CE) was the founder of the Karnat dynasty. He was a great warrior. Nanyadeva established Simraongarh as the capital of the Karnats. The rule of the Karnat dynasty (1097–1325 CE) is called the “Golden Age of Mithila.”

questions.q: Who was the last king of the Karnata dynasty?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The last ruler of the Karnat dynasty was Harisimha Deva. He was a patron of art and literature. He initiated the registration system.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Vikramshila University in Bihar : 1. It was located in the present-day Banka district of Bihar. 2. It was established by King Gopala I of the Pala dynasty. 3. The ‘Vajrayana’ sect of Buddhism flourished here. 4. Other subjects like Astronomy, Logic, Law, Grammar and Philosophy were also taught here. Which of the above statements are incorrect ?
questions.explanation: Vikramshila University (Mahavihara) was founded by the Pala ruler Dharmapala. It was located in the present-day Bhagalpur district of Bihar. Vajrayana, the Tantric branch of Buddhism, had the greatest influence in this university. Besides this, other subjects such as astronomy, logic, law, grammar and philosophy were also taught here. At the end of the 12th century, this university was destroyed by the army of Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khilji.

questions.q: Which ruler of Bengal founded the ancient University called ‘Vikramshila.’
questions.explanation: The ancient Buddhist university of Vikramshila was founded by Dharmapala (770–810 CE), a Pala ruler of Bengal. According to the Tibetan scholar Lama Taranatha, by the 10th century, Vikramshila had become an even larger center of learning than Nalanda University.
