options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Mountbatten announced that after Partition, the issues of the princely states falling in the two new countries—India and Pakistan—would be settled separately by “States Departments.” Nehru entrusted the responsibility of the “States Department” for the integration of the princely states to Sardar Patel. Sardar Patel took charge on 5 July, 1947, and V.P. Menon took charge as his Secretary.

questions.q: Who was the President of Indian National Congress at the time of Partition of India?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: At the time of the Partition of India (transfer of power), J.B. Kriplani was the President of the Indian National Congress. He became President in the Meerut Session in November, 1946, and remained President until November, 1947. After he resigned, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was made the President.

questions.q: Who presided over the Meerut Session of the Indian National Congress in the year 1947?
questions.explanation: At the time of the Partition of India (transfer of power), J.B. Kriplani was the President of the Indian National Congress. He became President in the Meerut Session in November, 1946, and remained President until November, 1947. After he resigned, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was made the President.

questions.q: Who was the Congress President at the time of the transfer of power to Indians by the British in the year 1947?
questions.explanation: At the time of the Partition of India (transfer of power), J.B. Kriplani was the President of the Indian National Congress. He became President in the Meerut Session in November, 1946, and remained President until November, 1947. After he resigned, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was made the President.

questions.q: The President of the Indian National Congress in the year 1947 was
questions.explanation: At the time of the Partition of India (transfer of power), J.B. Kriplani was the President of the Indian National Congress. He became President in the Meerut Session in November, 1946, and remained President until November, 1947. After he resigned, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was made the President.

questions.q: Which of the following political parties was in power in Britain at the time of India's independence?
questions.explanation: At the time of India’s independence, Clement R. Attlee was the British Prime Minister. His tenure was from 1945 to 1951. During that period, the Labour Party was in power in Britain. On 20 February, 1947, British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announced in the House of Commons that the British would leave India after transferring power to responsible hands, and that this would be done before June, 1948.

questions.q: In which year was the Regulating Act passed?
questions.explanation: To remove widespread corruption and misadministration in the Company, the British Parliament passed the Regulating Act, 1773. Under this, the Madras and Bombay Presidencies were brought under the Calcutta Presidency. The Governor of Bengal was now called the Governor-General of Bengal. Warren Hastings was made the first Governor-General of Bengal.

questions.q: The Regulating Act was passed in –
questions.explanation: To remove widespread corruption and misadministration in the Company, the British Parliament passed the Regulating Act, 1773. Under this, the Madras and Bombay Presidencies were brought under the Calcutta Presidency. The Governor of Bengal was now called the Governor-General of Bengal. Warren Hastings was made the first Governor-General of Bengal.

questions.q: Under which of the following acts did Lord Cornwallis get the right to overrule the decisions of his council?
questions.explanation: Cornwallis wanted to hold the powers of both the Governor- General and the Commander-in-Chief. According to the Act of 1786, this was accepted, and in special circumstances the Governor-General was also given the power to override the decisions of his Council and to enforce his own decision.

questions.q: When was the Pitt's India Act passed by the British Parliament?
questions.explanation: The Pitt’s India Act was passed in 1784 AD. The main provisions of the Pitt’s India Act, 1784 were the establishment of a Board of Control to supervise the Company’s civil, military and revenue affairs; reduction of the members of the Council of the Governor General in India to three members; and civil and military officers were asked to disclose details of their properties in India and Britain.

questions.q: Which Act provided for the competitive exam system for Civil Services?
questions.explanation: In the Charter Act, 1853, it was provided that the salaries of the Board of Control and its other officers would be fixed by the government; however, the Company would pay them. The number of Directors was reduced from 24 to 18, out of which 6 were to be nominated by the Crown. It also provided that appointments would now be made through competitive examinations, without any kind of discrimination.

questions.q: The post of the Indian High Commission was created by which Act?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the Government of India Act, 1919, a provision was made for appointing an Indian High Commissioner to reduce the workload of the Secretary of State for India. Its functions included purchasing arms and other goods for the Government of India, awarding contracts, looking after commercial interests, and taking care of Indian students studying in England, etc. The expenditure on the salaries of the High Commissioner and his assistants was to be met from India’s resources.

questions.q: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report formed the basis of the–
questions.explanation: The report of Edwin Montagu (then Secretary of State for India) and Viceroy Lord Chelmsford became the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919. Under this Act, dyarchy was introduced in the provinces for the first time.

questions.q: Who was the Prime Minister of England when the Montagu-Chelmsford Act was passed in 1919?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In 1919, when the Montagu–Chelmsford Act was passed, David Lloyd George was the Prime Minister of the U.K. He remained the Prime Minister of the U.K. from 1916 to 1922.

questions.q: About which Act, Jawaharlal Nehru had said, "We were provided with a car with all brakes and no engine"?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: About the Act of 1935, Jawaharlal Nehru said, “A car that has brakes but no engine.” He served as the Prime Minister of India from 1947 to 1964. He was a leading proponent of Panchsheel and believed in non-alignment.

questions.q: Which Act is not the landmark in the development of the Constitution during the British Rule?

options.D: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: During British rule in India, the British Government passed the Regulating Act, 1773; the Charter Act, 1833; and the Government of India Act, 1919, whereas the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 was passed by the Indian Parliament.

questions.q: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as a ‘Charter of Slavery’?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In his presidential address at the annual session of the Congress held at Lucknow, on 12 April 1936, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru called the Government of India Act, 1935 the “Charter of Slavery.” This Act provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation in which both British Indian provinces and Indian States (Princely States) were to be included, though this federation could never actually come into existence. Under this Act, there was also a provision for a bicameral legislature at the Centre.

questions.q: Government of India Act, 1935 abolished-
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished provincial dyarchy and introduced provincial autonomy. As a result, the distinction between reserved and transferred subjects ended. With some reservations, responsible government was established in the provinces.

questions.q: Which of the following was not one of the features of the Government of India Act, 1935?

options.A: Reconstruction of the Governor General's Executive Council

questions.explanation: The features of the Government of India Act, 1935 included the proposal of an Indian Federation, reorganization of the Governor-General’s Executive Council, and provincial autonomy; however, there was no provision for an evaluation of the Act of 1935. This Act also provided for the establishment of a Federal Court, division of powers between the Centre and the Provinces, a bicameral Central Legislature, abolition of dyarchy in the provinces, and dyarchy at the Centre, etc. India’s present constitutional structure is largely based on the Act of 1935.

questions.q: Which Act provided for the partition of India into two new dominions -India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament, formally approved the partition of British India and provided the legal basis for the creation of two new independent dominions/states—India and Pakistan. This Act received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947, and it provided that from 15 August 1947 the two independent dominions/states India and Pakistan would come into existence.

questions.q: Who is considered the father of dyarchy?

options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Sir Lionel Curtis is regarded as the father of dyarchy. His ideas related to dyarchy formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.

questions.q: The Muddiman Committee was appointed to report on the working of which of the following?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The Muddiman Committee was appointed in the year 1924 under the leadership of Sir Alexander Muddiman. This committee was appointed to discuss and examine the issue of dyarchy under the constitution established under the Government of India Act, 1919. Apart from the British members, it also had six Indian members—Shivswami Iyer, R. P. Paranjpye, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Bijoy/Vijay Chand Mahtab, Muhammad Shafi, and Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The committee submitted its report in the year 1925.

questions.q: Name the Principal of M.A.O. College, Aligarh, who encouraged Muslim Communalism in the last decades of the 19th Century?
questions.explanation: M.A.O. College (Mohammadan Anglo-Oriental College), Aligarh, was founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. In the last decades of the 19th century, the ‘Muslim separatist’ tendencies that emerged here were encouraged by several persons, among whom the Principal of M.A.O. College, Aligarh, Theodore Beck, was prominent.

questions.q: Consider the following events of Modern Indian History 1. Death sentence to Raja Nand Kumar 2. Treaty of Salbai 3. Battle of Wandiwash 4. Death of Tipu Sultan Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the above envents?
questions.explanation: The accepted years of these four events are as follows— Battle of Wandiwash – This was the decisive battle fought between the British and the French during the Third Carnatic War, which took place in 1760. This is the earliest event among the four. Death sentence to Raja Nandakumar – Raja Nandakumar, a high Brahmin of Bengal and former Diwan, was tried on the charge of forgery and hanged. This incident took place in 1775 in Calcutta. Treaty of Salbai – The agreement between the East India Company and the Marathas at the end of the First Anglo- Maratha War (1775–1782) is called the Treaty of Salbai. This treaty took place in 1782. Death of Tipu Sultan – Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore, was killed in the Battle of Srirangapatna during the Fourth Anglo–Mysore War (1799).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom?

options.A: She reigned for 70 years and died at the age of 96.
options.B: She reigned for 68 years and died at the age of 94.
options.C: She ruled for 72 years and died at the age of 92.
options.D: She ruled for 66 years and died at the age of 90.

questions.explanation: On 8 September, 2022, Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom died at the age of 96. In the year 1952, Elizabeth II assumed the throne of the United Kingdom. Thus, she reigned for 70 years, 214 days (6 February, 1952 – 8 September, 2022). Therefore, as the closest answer, option (a) can be selected.

questions.q: Queen Victoria was appointed the Empress of India in –
questions.explanation: The Royal Titles Act, 1876 was passed by the British Parliament in April, 1876. Under this Act, Queen Victoria was proclaimed the Empress of India at the Delhi Durbar on 1 January, 1877. Similarly, Emperor Edward VII was proclaimed Emperor of India in the year 1903, and George V in the year 1911.

questions.q: Under the Royal Titles Act, Queen Victoria became the Empress of India in
questions.explanation: The Royal Titles Act, 1876 was passed by the British Parliament in April, 1876. Under this Act, Queen Victoria was proclaimed the Empress of India at the Delhi Durbar on 1 January, 1877. Similarly, Emperor Edward VII was proclaimed Emperor of India in the year 1903, and George V in the year 1911.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.A: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was the pioneer of modern education.
options.B: Swami Dayanand proclaimed India for Indians.
options.C: Vivekananda participated in the Parliament of World Religions.
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati gave the slogan “India for Indians.” Swami Vivekananda participated in the “Parliament of the World’s Religions” held in Chicago in 1893. Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a pioneer of modern education. Therefore, option (d) is correct.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to resist the political reforms?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was the first Indian to raise a voice/ protest for political reforms. He wrote several articles on human rights and the development of democratic values. Bipin Chandra Pal wrote that the message of political freedom in India was first given by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. Some historians consider Surendranath Banerjee to be the first Indian to lead a movement for political reforms.

questions.q: Who first raised the demand for 'complete independence' in the year 1921?
questions.explanation: The Congress session held at Ahmedabad in 1921 was presided over by Hakim Ajmal Khan, as C. R. Das was in jail. In this session, Maulana Hasrat Mohani first raised the demand for “Complete Independence,” but Gandhiji opposed this demand and it was rejected.

questions.q: The slogans of the French Revolution - liberty, equality and inspired the whole world.
questions.explanation: The slogan of Equality, Liberty and Fraternity (Brotherhood) is a contribution of the French Revolution, which influenced not only France but the whole world. It is noteworthy that the French Revolution began on 14 July 1789. At that time, the King of France was Louis XVI.

questions.q: Who was the most bitter critic of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Jamaluddin Afghani was the most bitter critic of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. Sir Syed started one of the most influential movements in favour of English education and cooperation with the British government. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan opposed the establishment of the Congress and, along with Raja Shiv Prasad Singh of Banaras, founded the “United Indian Patriotic Association” in 1888.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is correct? i. 1905 — Partition of Bengal ii. 1908 - Split in Congress iii. 1919 - Rowlatt Satyagraha
questions.explanation: The Partition of Bengal took place in 1905 and the Rowlatt Satyagraha took place in 1919. The split in Congress (Congress division) took place in the Surat session of 1907. Therefore, only pairs (i) and (iii) are correctly matched.

questions.q: Presided over the Banaras Hindu Mahasabha session of August, 1923-
questions.explanation: Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya was among the most eminent leaders of the Hindu Mahasabha, and he presided over the Hindu Mahasabha session held at Banaras in 1923. In the same Banaras session, movements such as the Shuddhi movement were welcomed. He began the publication of ‘Abhyudaya’ (in Hindi) and ‘The Leader’ (in English), and he also served as editor of newspapers such as ‘Hindustan’ and ‘The Indian Union’.

questions.q: Who was the secretary of Mahatma Gandhi during Noakhali?
questions.explanation: During the phase of violence in the Noakhali region of Bengal, Mahatma Gandhi’s personal secretary was the famous Bengali anthropologist and Gandhian leader Nirmal Kumar Bose. He also worked as Mahatma Gandhi’s interpreter in Bengal. He remained Mahatma Gandhi’s personal secretary till 1946–47.

questions.q: The Bombay Plan proposed:

options.A: A rapid rate of economic growth
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The ‘Bombay Plan’ was presented in 1944 by a group of leading Indian industrialists. Under this plan, rapid economic growth of the Indian economy was advocated through proposals based on import substitution and industrialisation. At the same time, it reflected the need for state intervention and planned development in the country’s economic development, along with the need for public sector undertakings, which shows an abandonment of some capitalist features. On this basis, the correct answer will be option (e).

questions.q: In which year the first Census was introduced in India?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: During British rule, the first census was conducted in 1872 during the time of Lord Mayo; however, the first regular census, i.e., the beginning of continuous decennial census, is considered from 1881 during the time of Lord Ripon.

questions.q: Which Dogra general led successful military campaigns in Ladakh, Baltistan, and parts of Tibet between 1834 and 1841?
questions.explanation: Zorawar Singh, the commander-in-chief of Dogra ruler Gulab Singh of Jammu and Kashmir and the Governor of Kishtwar, led successful military campaigns in Ladakh, Baltistan and some parts of Tibet between 1834 and 1841. He was killed in battle during the Western Tibet campaign (1841). Under the Treaty of Amritsar (March 1846), the colonial rulers sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh rupees. Maharaja Gulab Singh unified Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? I. Laik Ali was the President of the Nizam's Executive Council. II. 'Operation Polo' against Hyderabad lasted for 48 hours. III. The state of Kashmir signed the Instrument of Accession on 15-08-1947. IV. Shah Nawaz Bhutto was the last Diwan of Junagadh State. V. K.M. Munshi was appointed by the Government of India as its agent in Hyderabad.

options.D: I, II, III and IV only
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Mir Laik Ali was the President of the Nizam’s Executive Council (the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad during the Nizam’s rule). ‘Operation Polo’ for Hyderabad’s merger with India took about five days in September 1948. The Maharaja of Kashmir, Hari Singh, signed the Instrument of Accession with India on 26 October 1947. Shah Nawaz Bhutto was the last Diwan of the Junagadh State. K.M. Munshi was appointed by the Government of India as its Agent General in the Hyderabad State. Thus, among the given statements, only I, IV and V are correct.

questions.q: "So long as this third power, i.e. England is here, our communal differences would keep on troubling us" Who said this?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The above statement was made by Mahatma Gandhi in an interview with Louis Fischer.

questions.q: Consider the following events during India’s Freedom Struggle : 1. Home Rule Movement 2. Surat Split 3. Kheda Satyagraha 4. Minto-Morley Reforms Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the events given above?
questions.explanation: Event — Year Surat Split — 1907 Minto–Morley Reforms — 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms) Home Rule Movement — 1916 Kheda Satyagraha — 1918

questions.q: The objective of the 'Antyodaya' program is -

options.C: Helping the poorest of the poor

questions.explanation: The objective of the Antyodaya Programme is to help the poorest among the poor. The idea of Antyodaya was propounded by Mahatma Gandhi. He treated the benefit to the poorest/weakest person in society as the yardstick for judging any step or policy. This “last person–centred” thought is the core of the Antyodaya concept. However, the credit for making the idea or philosophy of Antyodaya widely popular goes to Shyama Prasad Mukherjee.

questions.q: “He was a great unifier in India who taught us not only bare tolerance of others but the willing acceptance of them as our friends and comrades in common undertakings” who said it?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The given statement is by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, in which he said this about Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.q: Who among the following capitalists served as an AICC Treasurer for many years and went to jail in 1930?
questions.explanation: Seth Jamnalal Bajaj was among the close associates of Gandhiji. He remained the Treasurer of the All India Congress Committee (AICC) for a long time. He went to jail for participating in the Nagpur Flag Satyagraha (1923) and again during the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930).

questions.q: Ambabai, a woman freedom fighter, belonged to which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Ambabai was born in 1889 in the then princely state of Mysore (now Karnataka) in an orthodox Brahmin family. She played an important role in the freedom movement in South India. She also led sit-in protests in Udupi against shops selling foreign clothes and liquor.

questions.q: Which among the following year Surendra Nath Banerjee was eliminated from Indian Civil Services?

options.E: None of the above/ More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Surendranath Banerjee was the second Indian to pass the Indian Civil Service examination. His first posting was as an Assistant Magistrate in Sylhet (present-day Bangladesh). Due to procedural irregularities, he was removed from service in 1874 A.D.

questions.q: “Therefore, the Government of India always acts with consent and often on the instructions of the Chamber of Commerce, and this is called 'White Man's Burden'.” Who said this?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The given statement was made by Sachchidanand Sinha.

questions.q: Who became champion of socialism and wanted to overthrow British rule, Princely states, landlordism and Capitalism in 1933?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was a supporter of socialism. In 1933, he wanted to uproot British rule, princely states, zamindari, and capitalism. Nehru’s socialism was influenced by Soviet socialism. He visited the Soviet Union in November 1927.

questions.q: How did the study of history help in creating a feeling of nationalism in India towards the end of the 19th century?

options.A: Urging people to change the miserable conditions under British rule and to struggle
options.B: By reinterpreting history and refuting the British portrayal of Indians as backward, primitive, and incapable of governing themselves
options.C: By writing about India's glorious past and urging people to be proud of their achievements
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: All the statements given in the options show how the study of history helped create a sense of nationalism in India at the end of the 19th century.

questions.q: Arrange the following events in chronological order during British rule:' A. Dandi March B. Simon Commission C. Poona Pact D. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
questions.explanation: The years of the events are as follows— Dandi March — 1930 Simon Commission (formation) — 1927 Poona Pact — 1932 Gandhi–Irwin Pact — 1931 Accordingly, the correct chronological order is B A D C, which matches option (b).

questions.q: February 1927 marked a turning point in Jawaharlal's 'intellectual development' with his active participation in the Brussels Congress against colonial repression and imperialism." Who wrote these words?'

options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: “…… a turning point came in Jawaharlal’s ‘intellectual development’ when he actively participated against colonial oppression and imperialism at the Brussels Congress in February 1927.” This statement is by S. Gopal.

questions.q: Which of the following events happened first?

options.A: Resolution of the Quit India Movement
options.C: Arrival of Lord Wavell as the Governor General
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Events Year (1) Arrival of the Cripps Mission March 1942 (2) Resolution of the Quit India Movement August 1942 (3) Arrival of Lord Wavell as Governor-General October 1943 (4) Arrival of the Cabinet Mission March 1946 Therefore, among the given events, the earliest was the arrival of the Cripps Mission under the leadership of Stafford Cripps.

questions.q: Match the following: (A) Bardoli 1. Maharashtra (B) Chauri-Chaura 2. Gujarat (C) Yerwada 3. West Bengal (D) Noakhali 4. Uttar Pradesh Code: A B C D
questions.explanation: Bardoli is located in the state of Gujarat. Chauri-Chaura is presently located in Uttar Pradesh. It was here that during the Non-Cooperation Movement, on 4 February 1922, a violent mob set a police station on fire, in which 23 policemen were killed. Saddened by this incident, Gandhiji withdrew the Non- Cooperation Movement on 12 February 1922. Yerwada Jail is located in Maharashtra. At present, Noakhali is a part of Bangladesh, not the state of West Bengal. Before the partition of India, it was a part of the Bengal Province.

questions.q: First Indian elected to the British House of Commons was Dadabhai Naoroji who contested on the ticket of:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji (1825–1917) formed the London Indian Society in 1865 along with W. C. Banerjee. Its main objective was to increase political and social awareness among Indian students in England and to place India’s problems before the British public and the government. In 1892, he became the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons on the ticket of the Liberal Party. In his book “Poverty and Un-British Rule in India”, Dadabhai Naoroji clearly highlighted India’s economic distress during British rule, and he was the first to propound the Drain of Wealth, that is, the Drain Theory.

questions.q: Who among the following became India’s unofficial ambassador to England?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji is known as India’s unofficial ambassador in England. With the objective of conveying the Indian viewpoint to the British public, he founded the East India Association in 1866.

questions.q: Which famous Indian was known as 'Gurudev'?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore was born in the city of Calcutta on 7 May 1861. In 1901, he started a school at Santiniketan called the Brahmacharya Ashram. On 23 December 1918, Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore laid the foundation of Visva-Bharati. In 1913, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for the English translation of his collection of songs “Gitanjali”, titled “Song Offerings”. He was known as “Gurudev”.

questions.q: Who gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan'?
questions.explanation: The famous slogan “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” was given by India’s former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri.

questions.q: Which woman made the most significant contribution to Indian politics after 1947?
questions.explanation: Aruna Asaf Ali was a nationalist and a freedom fighter. In the Quit India Movement of 1942, she and Sucheta Kriplani were two leading women organisers of the underground movement. After 1947, Aruna Asaf Ali joined the Socialist Party in 1948. In the 1950s, she joined the Communist Party of India and visited Moscow (Russia). In 1954, she was a collaborator in the formation of the National Federation of Indian Women. In 1958, she became the Mayor of Delhi, and in 1958 she also founded the newspaper ‘Patriot’. In this way, she made the maximum contribution to Indian politics after 1947.

questions.q: Name the scholar of Deoband who played an important role in the freedom movement:
questions.explanation: Abul Kalam Azad was associated with the Deoband movement. ‘Mazameen al-Nadwa’, a collection of articles written by Abul Kalam Azad, was published in the Urdu magazine ‘Al Nadwa’. He served as the President of the Indian National Congress from 1940 to 1946. ‘India Wins Freedom’ is his famous book.

questions.q: What was the common relationship between Katherine Mayo, Aldous Huxley, Charles Andrews and William Digby?

options.A: They wrote commentaries on the condition of India during the British rule
options.B: They were supporters of the Indian National Movement
options.C: They were opponents of the Indian National Movement
options.D: They were friends of Mahatma Gandhi

questions.explanation: Katherine Mayo, Aldous Huxley, Charles Andrews and William Digby wrote comments on India’s condition during British rule. Katherine Mayo was the author of ‘Mother India’, and William Digby wrote ‘Prosperous British India’. Charles Andrews was born in 1871 in England. He was a friend of Mahatma Gandhi. He came to India in 1904 and taught at St. Stephen’s College. He encouraged Indian nationalism through his books and journalism. Aldous Huxley travelled to India in the first half of the 20th century and, in his travelogue, wrote about the conditions of India at that time.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is correct?

options.D: Shyamji Krishna Varma- Founder of India House in Paris
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Under the Individual Satyagraha Movement started by Mahatma Gandhi in 1940, Vinoba Bhave was made the first individual satyagrahi and Jawaharlal Nehru was made the second individual satyagrahi. Chittaranjan Das (C.R. Das) was a famous Indian leader, politician, lawyer, and a major leader of the Indian freedom movement. He was given the title ‘Deshbandhu’. The Surat session of the Congress held in 1907 was presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh, whereas William Wedderburn was elected as the Congress President in 1889 and 1910. In 1905, Shyamji Krishna Varma established India House in London.

questions.q: Who was the leader of the Non-Aligned Movement?
questions.explanation: The Non-Aligned Movement was started on India’s initiative. It may be noted that, to establish peace and mutual cooperation in the world, India’s Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, Egypt’s President Colonel Nasser, Ghana’s President Kwame Nkrumah, Indonesia’s President Sukarno, and Yugoslavia’s President Marshal Tito Josip Broz, with mutual cooperation, initiated the Non-Aligned Movement as a third force in world politics. The first summit of the non-aligned countries was held in Belgrade under the chairmanship of Yugoslavia’s President Marshal Tito. The 19th summit of the Non-Aligned Movement was held in January 2024 in Kampala (Uganda).

questions.q: Which principle did Nehru present to establish world peace and mutual cooperation?
questions.explanation: The Non-Aligned Movement was started on India’s initiative. It may be noted that, to establish peace and mutual cooperation in the world, India’s Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, Egypt’s President Colonel Nasser, Ghana’s President Kwame Nkrumah, Indonesia’s President Sukarno, and Yugoslavia’s President Marshal Tito Josip Broz, with mutual cooperation, initiated the Non-Aligned Movement as a third force in world politics. The first summit of the non-aligned countries was held in Belgrade under the chairmanship of Yugoslavia’s President Marshal Tito. The 19th summit of the Non-Aligned Movement was held in January 2024 in Kampala (Uganda).

questions.q: Mother Teresa’s birthplace was—
questions.explanation: Mother Teresa was a citizen of Albanian origin. She was born on 26 August 1910 in the city of Skopje, in present-day North Macedonia. In 1929, she came to Kolkata. questions.q: Which one of the following books was written by Tilak?

questions.q: Consider the following statements about festivals and fairs in India. 1. questions.q: Which of the following temples is located in Kanchipuram?
questions.explanation: Ekambareswarar Temple is located in Kanchipuram. This temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva. The construction of this temple was carried out by the Pallavas. questions.q: Which of the following is a classical dance form of the state of Assam?
questions.explanation: Assam’s classical dance is Sattriya. This dance form is devotional in nature because its purpose was to propagate Neo-Vaishnavism. It was introduced by the great Vaishnav saint of Assam and reformer, Mahapurush Srimanta Shankaradeva. It is one of India’s eight classical dances.

questions.q: ‘Maghar Mahotsav’ was started in honor of Sant Kabir, in the year-

questions.q: The world's largest stadium is located in-

questions.q: The 'Statue of Liberty' is located in-
questions.explanation: The 'Statue of Liberty' was made in France. The sculptor of the Statue of Liberty was Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi. The architect of the pedestal on which it is installed was Richard Morris Hunt, and the engineer of the internal framework was Alexandre Gustave Eiffel. As a symbol of France–America friendship, France gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States on 28 October 1886, on the occasion of the centenary of American independence. This statue is located on Liberty Island in New York Harbor.

questions.q: In July, 2019, experts visited for the first documentation of a Megalithic site of Bihar in which of the following districts?

questions.q: The oldest culture from Chirand of Bihar is

questions.explanation: From the archaeological site named Chirand in Saran district of Bihar, the Neolithic culture has come to light. questions.q: Chinese traveller I-Tsing was on the tour of Bihar in about:

questions.q: Patna was made the provincial capital by-

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In 1855–56, the Santhal rebellion mainly took place against British rule. Their main complaint was against the bhadralog (civilized people), i.e., the respectable people of Bengal and North India who came and settled in their area and exploited them. When the tribals complained to the British, the British supported those bhadralog. The tribals called their exploiters diku. questions.q: Who led the revolt of 1857 in Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In 1857, the revolt at Jagdishpur was led by Kunwar Singh, who belonged to Arrah (Bhojpur district) in Bihar. He raised the banner of revolt against the British. Nature had endowed him with indomitable courage, bravery, and the ideal qualities of a military leader; therefore, he is rightly regarded as the “Lion of Bihar” during the revolt. He overthrew British authority in the then Shahabad and established his own government. He moved towards Kalpi to help Nana Saheb for a joint attack on Kanpur. He carried the flame of revolt to Rohtas, Mirzapur, Rewa, Banda and Lucknow, where he was welcomed with great respect. As his final success, he badly defeated the British near his hometown Jagdishpur. During this battle, he was severely injured after being defeated by the British commander William Taylor, and he attained martyrdom on 26 April, 1858. However, in some sources the date of his death is given as 9 May, 1858, which is erroneous.

questions.q: The person who led the agitation in Bihar for the separate state whereby in the year 1911 new provinces Bihar and Odisha were formed was-
questions.explanation: In 1907, Mahesh Narayan passed away. He used to publish a newspaper named Bihar Times. Through this newspaper, Mahesh Narayan put forward the demand for Bihar’s separation. The separation movement gained momentum across Bihar. After Mahesh Narayan’s death, Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha became the main leader of this movement. A demand was raised to grant Bihar the status of a separate state by separating it from Bengal, which was accepted at the Durbar held in Delhi on 12 December, 1911. Brahmadev Prasad, Ali Imam, Mazharul Haq and Hasan Imam also joined Dr. Sinha. In 1908–09, the Bihar Provincial Conference was organised. On 1 April, 1912, the new province of Bihar and Orissa emerged after being separated from Bengal, with Patna as its capital. Under the Government of India Act, 1935, Orissa was separated from Bihar on 1 April, 1936 and made a new province. Therefore, the formation of Bihar as a separate Indian province became effective from 1 April, 1936.

questions.explanation: Under the Tinkathia system, the farmers of the Champaran region of Bihar were compelled to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land. At the invitation of Rajkumar Shukla of Champaran during the annual session of the Congress held in Lucknow in 1916, Mahatma Gandhi came to Champaran in April 1917. questions.explanation: Sheelbhadra Yajee was a freedom fighter from Bihar, who was associated with Mahatma Gandhi and Subhash Chandra Bose. Yajee joined Subhash Chandra Bose for the establishment of the All India Forward Bloc and also remained associated with the I.N.A. movement.

questions.q: Which village was Ramchandra Sharma from?
questions.explanation: Ramchandra Sharma was a resident of Amhara (Patna). He was a prominent leader of the Forward Bloc in Bihar.

questions.q: When was the Patna College established?
questions.explanation: Patna College was established in 1863 A.D. It is known as the oldest institution of higher education in Bihar, and it is important both historically and academically.

questions.q: In 1940, Patna Women's College was established by which of the following societies?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Patna Women’s College is the first institution of higher education in Bihar opened to meet the educational needs of women. Bishop B. J. Sullivan, S.J., the Bishop of Patna (founder), and Mother M. Josephine, A.C., the Superior General of the Apostolic Carmel, named it Patna Women’s College and presented it as a gift for the women of Bihar. At present, Patna Women’s College is run by the Sisters of the Apostolic Carmel. The Apostolic Carmel was founded in 1868 in France, and in India it was established in 1870.

questions.q: Who laid the foundation stone of National College and Bihar Vidyapith?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi laid the foundation stone of National College and Bihar Vidyapith. Bihar Vidyapith was inaugurated by Gandhiji in February, 1921.

questions.q: In Bihar though 'Zamindari' was statutorily abolished in 1952, the social base of land control remained in the grip of
questions.explanation: In 1950, the Bihar government passed the “Bihar Land Reforms Act”, whose validity was upheld by the Supreme Court (except sections 4(b) and 23(F). Amendments were made in 1954 and 1959. However, the Act had certain provisions under which a large portion of land could be retained by the landlords for purposes such as house, garden, pond, library, business, etc. Moreover, due to slow implementation of the law, control over land continued to remain with the dominant castes.

questions.q: Who is considered the creator of modern Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sachchidanand Sinha was a noted Indian politician, educationist, lawyer, and journalist. He is regarded as the “maker of modern Bihar.” He was the driving force behind the movement for the separation of Bihar from Bengal, and the formation of the Bihar and Orissa Province was the result of his tireless efforts. Sachchidanand Sinha was made the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December, 1946 in the Central Hall of the Parliament House under the chairmanship of Sachchidanand Sinha. Besides this, Bihar’s first Chief Minister Dr. Shri Krishna Singh is also called the “Creator of Modern Bihar.”

questions.q: Sachchidananda Sinha was associated with :
questions.explanation: Sachchidananda Sinha was not associated with any of the above movements. He was unanimously chosen as the temporary chairman at the first sitting of the Constituent Assembly (9 December, 1946).

questions.q: Which one of the following was not a dominant caste in pre-independence Bihar?
questions.explanation: In pre-independence Bihar, Bhumihars, Rajputs and Kayasthas were dominant castes, whereas the Kurmi caste was not dominant.

questions.q: “It will be our blunder if we leave the people of Bihar and their Government unsafe before the violence and uncivilized attacks of League leaders.” In the year 1946 who told this?
questions.explanation: The statement in the question was made by Sardar Patel in 1946 during the communal riots in Bihar.
